fills.researcher_notes: UNRESOLVED. Existence and current spec are solidly confirmed -- SNGPL's own FY2018 asset register ('TRANSMISSION SYSTEM As at June 30, 2018', SNGPLAR-2018.pdf, printed p.33, row 56) lists 'AV22 - KOT ADDU / 16 / 69.65' km MAINLINE, an EXACT match to this row's Diameter (16) and LengthKnown (69.65) (verifier FAILs on this large 186pp/4MB PDF -- documented large-PDF false-negative pattern, manually confirmed via pdftotext -layout). The same table shows a second, larger loopline on the identical corridor -- row 57 'AV22-KOT ADDU / 20 / 38.01' km looplinke -- so this is a real, twice-built corridor, not a mapping artifact. But no source found names a year for either build. Kot Addu is the site of the Kot Addu Power Company (KAPCO) plant, built in five phases between 1985 and 1996 (KAPCO's own 'About Us' page, kapco.com.pk/?page_id=22), which is the obvious reason SNGPL would need a delivery spur here -- but sources disagree on which KAPCO phase/year the plant itself reached full capacity (worldpowerplants.com says 'commissioned 1996'; power-technology.com says 'got commissioned in 1987'), and none of the KAPCO-side or SNGPL-side sources I found ties the SPECIFIC 16in/69.65km AV22-Kot Addu spur to a year -- it could predate KAPCO (an existing SNGPL Punjab distribution corridor that KAPCO later tapped) or postdate an early KAPCO phase. Searched: SNGPL Annual Report 2017 MILESTONES timeline (no Kot Addu-specific entry among its 16 numbered projects), SNGPL Annual Report 2018 fixed-asset/Musharaka notes (no 'Kot Addu' cost-basis line item, only an unrelated 'Repeater Station Kot Addu' equipment entry), general web search for 'AV22 Kot Addu SNGPL pipeline year' (no results naming a construction date). Recommend leaving StartYear1 blank/UNRESOLVED rather than inferring a KAPCO-phase year with no direct textual link to this specific pipe.
